facts.text: Crypto prices continue to surge this morning, hitting levels last seen in January of this year.
This morning's opening price for bitcoin and ethereum both mark gains of over 10% in the last week and month.
Here's a look at how the opening bitcoin price has changed versus last week, month, and year:
The price of ethereum this morning, Tuesday, September 22, 2026 , was 5% higher than Monday's open.
Bitcoin, ethereum, and other cryptocurrencies are rapidly evolving.
Follow the latest developments from Yahoo Finance and others here .
Another major factor in the crypto price surge is short liquidations.
This is from a Coinpedia article from September 21:
Bitcoin led the liquidations with $421.5 million, while Ethereum followed with $180.31 million.
In the latest hour alone, liquidations reached $634.62 million, with about 84% coming from short positions.
Keep reading: Why Is the Crypto Market Up Today?
Bitcoin's price has swung sharply in recent months.
Here's how to buy and store bitcoin as safely as possible.
Here's your beginner-friendly guide to the blockchain, smart contracts, DeFi, and how ETH differs from Bitcoin.

Crypto liquidations have surged to $602 million over the last 24 hours, per data from CoinGlass , with Ethereum flipping Bitcoin to become the biggest contributor with $187 million in liquidations compared to $184 million for BTC.
Overall, short liquidations make up $400 million of the pile.
Bitcoin topped the $62,000 mark Thursday morning for the first time in more than a week, rebounding to $62,078 after falling to a 21-month low under $58,000 earlier in the week.
Stocks are mixed following the news, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq both down for the day, but the Dow still green, per Yahoo Finance .
The bullish rebound comes following comments Wednesday from Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh, who declined to say whether the agency planned rate hikes later this year.

As of this writing, interest rate traders foresee roughly even odds of the Fed either holding rates steady or raising them at its September meeting, though they project a 64% chance of some kind of rate hike by the FOMC's October meeting, per CME's FedWatch .
